bio: Darren Bailey (born March 17, 1966) is an American politician who was a Republican member of the Illinois Senate for the 55th District and previously a member of the Illinois House of Representatives for the 109th District in Southern Illinois.
offices: Member of the Illinois House of Representatives (2019–2021)
Member of the State Senate of Illinois (2021–2023)

items.t: Is pro-life and has voted against abortion rights measures as a state lawmaker.
items.q: He opposes abortion, and as a state lawmaker, he has voted against abortion rights measures.

items.t: Praised the Supreme Court's 2022 decision to overturn Roe v. Wade.
items.q: He praised the Supreme Court's 2022 decision to overturn Roe v. Wade.

items.t: Supports a statewide ban on abortion except when the mother's life is in danger, including in cases of rape or incest.
items.q: He supports a statewide ban on abortion except in cases where the mother's life is in danger, opposing abortion in cases of rape or incest.

items.t: Sued Governor Pritzker over the extension of the COVID-19 stay-at-home order (2020).
items.q: In April 2020, Bailey sued Governor JB Pritzker, claiming that the governor's stay-at-home order extension to mitigate effects of the COVID-19 pandemic was unfairly affecting residents of Clay County.

items.t: Is against the SAFE-T Act, which ended mandatory cash bail in Illinois.
items.q: Bailey strongly opposes the SAFE-T Act, a bill signed into law by Governor J. B. Pritzker that, among other things, ended mandatory cash bail in Illinois.

items.t: Sponsored a 2019 resolution calling for the City of Chicago to become its own state.
items.q: In 2019, Bailey and seven other Republicans sponsored a resolution calling for the City of Chicago to become its own state
